module2_lower.stem: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to (u⁻³v⁴w⁴)(u⁴w⁵ + v⁷w⁻⁷) ?
module2_lower.rationale: u⁻³v⁴w⁴ multiplies each term inside the parentheses, and the exponents of each variable add.
reasons: multiplied only the first term inside the parentheses by the monomial
left v out of both products because it is missing from one factor of each
kept only the variables that both factors carry, dropping v from the first product and u from the second

module2_lower.stem: A shipping service restricts the dimensions of the boxes it will ship for a certain type of service. The restriction states that for boxes shaped like rectangular prisms, the sum of the perimeter of the base of the box and the height of the box cannot exceed 170 inches. The perimeter of the base is determined using the width and length of the box. If a box has a height of 70 inches and its length is 3 times the width, which inequality shows the allowable width x, in inches, of the box?
module2_lower.rationale: The base has perimeter 2(x + 3x) = 8x, so 8x + 70 ≤ 170, leaving x ≤ 12 1/2; a width is positive, so 0 < x ≤ 12 1/2.
reasons: doubled the length but counted the width only once
added the width and the length once each instead of finding the whole perimeter
left the height out of the cap altogether

module2_upper.stem:
(d − 6) + (3d + 8)
Which of the following expressions is equivalent to the expression above?
module2_upper.rationale: Like terms are collected power by power.
reasons: added every coefficient and every exponent as if all the terms were alike
added the exponents as well as the coefficients
multiplied the coefficients of the like terms instead of adding them

module2_upper.stem: A geologist estimates that the volume of a slab of basalt is greater than 16.4 cubic feet but less than 19.1 cubic feet. The geologist also estimates that the slab of basalt weighs 280 pounds per cubic foot of volume. Which inequality represents this situation, where x represents the estimated total weight, in pounds, of the slab of basalt?
module2_upper.rationale: Each cubic foot weighs 280 pounds, so the smallest total is 280(16.4) and the largest is 280(19.1); multiplying by a positive number keeps the two ends in order, so 280(16.4) < x < 280(19.1).
reasons: divided by the quantity that should have been multiplied, which also turns the two ends round
subtracted the two quantities instead of multiplying them
added the two quantities instead of multiplying them

module2_upper.stem:
576r² − 1156
Which of the following expressions is equivalent to the expression above?
module2_upper.rationale: 576 is 24² and 1156 is 34², so the expression is r times 24 all squared minus 34 squared.
reasons: used the same sign in both brackets, which squares the first bracket instead
halved the two square roots instead of taking them
halved the two square roots and used the same sign in both brackets

module2_upper.stem: The average annual energy cost for a certain home is $3,488. The homeowner plans to spend $29,000 to install a geothermal heating system. The homeowner estimates that the average annual energy cost will then be $1,942. Which of the following inequalities can be solved to find t, the number of years after installation at which the total amount of energy cost savings will exceed the installation cost?
module2_upper.rationale: Each year saves 3,488 − 1,942 dollars, so t years save (3,488 − 1,942)t, and that has to pass the $29,000 it cost to install, so 29,000 < (3,488 − 1,942)t.
reasons: subtracted one year's old cost from the installation cost instead of finding the yearly saving
compared the two the wrong way round, so the saving never catches the installation cost up
divided the two annual costs instead of subtracting them

module2_upper.stem: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to (x⁻⁶y⁵z⁴)(x²z⁶ + y⁸z⁻⁷) ?
module2_upper.rationale: x⁻⁶y⁵z⁴ multiplies each term inside the parentheses, and the exponents of each variable add.
reasons: kept only the variables that both factors carry, dropping y from the first product and x from the second
multiplied only the first term inside the parentheses by the monomial
left y out of both products because it is missing from one factor of each

module2_upper.stem:
48G + 3R = 618
At a school fair, students can win colored tokens that are worth a different number of points depending on the color. One student won G green tokens and R red tokens worth a total of 618 points. The given equation represents this situation. How many more points is a red token worth than a green token?
module2_upper.rationale: G is a count of green tokens, so the 48 multiplying it is the points one green token carries, and likewise 3 for a red one.

module2_upper.stem:
x² − cx + 122 = 0
In the equation above, c is a constant and c > 0. If the equation has two integer solutions, what is a possible value of c ?
module2_upper.rationale: Two integer solutions multiply to 122, so they are 1 and 122, 2 and 61; c is their sum, which can be 63, 123.

module2_upper.stem:
y < −5x + 2
For which of the following tables are all the values of x and their corresponding values of y solutions to the given inequality?
module2_upper.rationale: At x = 3 the boundary is −13, and only one table keeps every value of y on the required side of the boundary at all three values of x.
reasons: put every value of y on the wrong side of the boundary line
used y = −5x + 2 itself, so every pair sits on the boundary line, which a strict inequality leaves out
checked the pair at x = 3 and stopped; the other two lie on the wrong side of the boundary line

module2_upper.stem: Which of the following is an equivalent form of (3t + 3)² − (6t² + 4) ?
module2_upper.rationale: (3t + 3)² is 9t² + 18t + 9, and every term of the second bracket is then subtracted.
reasons: doubled each term instead of squaring and then added the two constants rather than subtracting
doubled each term instead of squaring the binomial, so the middle term never appeared
subtracted the two constant terms the wrong way round

module2_upper.stem: In the xy-plane, a circle with a radius of 12 has center (−1, 12). Which of the following is an equation of the circle?
module2_upper.rationale: A circle with center (h, k) and radius r has equation (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r², which gives (x + 1)² + (y − 12)² = 144.
reasons: kept the signs of the center and used the radius instead of its square
used the radius itself instead of its square
kept the signs of the center's coordinates instead of changing them

module2_upper.stem:
p⁴ + p² − 6
Which of the following is equivalent to the expression above?
module2_upper.rationale: The constants in the two brackets have to multiply to −6 and add to 1; that second condition is what rules out the other factor pairs.
reasons: put the two signs on the wrong brackets
found a pair whose product is −6 but whose sum is 5, not 1
found a pair whose product is −6 but whose sum is −5, not 1

module2_upper.stem:
8x + 7y = 7
48x + 42y = 42
For each real number r, which of the following points lies on the graph of each equation in the xy-plane for the given system?
module2_upper.rationale: The second equation is the first multiplied by 6, so the two draw the same line and any point on it will do. Letting y be r and solving 8x + 7y = 7 for x gives every such point at once.
reasons: solved the equation for x but wrote that expression as the y-coordinate
solved for y but kept the sign of the x term, which changes the line
divided r by the multiplier between the two equations and used the two right-hand sides as the shifts

module2_upper.stem: Point X lies on a circle of radius 12 in the xy-plane and has coordinates (0, −12). Point O is the center of the circle and has coordinates (0, 0). module2_upper.rationale: Y must be (0, 12), the far end of the diameter through X, so angle XOY is a half turn plus any whole number of full turns: π + 30π = 31π.
reasons: a half-integer multiple of π stops a quarter turn away, at (12, 0)
an even multiple of π is a whole number of full turns, which ends back at X

read a mean off a display that does not show one: the box plot gives only the least value, the quartiles, the median and the greatest value
read the wider box as the larger average; a box plot shows five summary values, not the individual measurements a mean needs

module2_upper.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to (z² − 6z − 1)/(z + 9) ?
module2_upper.rationale: z² − 6z − 1 is (z + 9)(z − 15) + 134, and only 134 is left over.
reasons: subtracted the divisor's constant from the remainder instead of multiplying by it
used the divisor's constant with the wrong sign when finding the quotient
used the divisor's constant with the wrong sign, and then added the quotient's constant to the remainder instead of multiplying it by the divisor's root

module2_upper.stem: Maria is working this summer as part of a crew on a farm, and earned $7 per hour for the first 10 hours worked this week. Because of that performance, the crew leader raised the salary to $15 per hour for the rest of the week. Maria saves 90% of the earnings from each week. What is the least number of hours Maria must work the rest of the week to save at least $260 for the week?
module2_upper.rationale: The condition is 0.9(70 + 15n) ≥ 260. With n = 15 the savings is $265.50, which meets it, and with n = 14 it is $252.00, which does not, so the least whole number that works is 15.
reasons: multiplied the target by the savings fraction instead of dividing by it
applied the savings fraction twice, once to the target and once to the hourly pay
used the first block's hourly rate for the whole week and left out the money already earned

module2_upper.stem: Data set A consists of the heights of 56 plants and has a mean of 48 centimeters. Data set B consists of the heights of 56 plants and has a mean of 54 centimeters. Data set C consists of the heights of the 112 plants from data sets A and B. What is the mean, in centimeters, of data set C?
module2_upper.rationale: The two data sets total 2,688 and 3,024, so all 112 values total 5,712.

module1.stem: During spring migration, an arctic tern traveled a minimum of 87 miles and a maximum of 140 miles between stopover locations. Which inequality represents this situation, where d is a possible distance, in miles, this arctic tern traveled between stopover locations during spring migration?
module1.rationale: Every recorded value is at least the smallest, 87, and at most the largest, 140; both were recorded, so both ends belong to the range and 87 ≤ d ≤ 140.
reasons: used the largest recorded value as the bottom of the range and the sum of the two as the top
kept only the largest recorded value and read it as a floor rather than as the top of the range
kept only the smallest recorded value and read it as a cap rather than as the bottom of the range

module1.stem:
(k + 2) + (2k + 6)
Which of the following is equivalent to the given expression?
module1.rationale: Like terms are collected power by power.
reasons: multiplied the coefficients of the like terms instead of adding them
subtracted the constant terms instead of adding them
lined the terms up as written and added the exponents too

module1.stem: Tobias scored 98, 87, and 81 on the first three exams in chemistry class. Solving which inequality gives the score, G, on Tobias's fourth exam that will result in a mean score on all four exams of at least 90 ?
module1.rationale: The mean of the four scores is the sum divided by 4, and that mean has to be at least 90, so (G + 98 + 87 + 81)/4 ≥ 90.
reasons: multiplied the unknown score by 4 instead of dividing the whole total by it
left the unknown score out of the sum being averaged
subtracted the three known scores from the target mean instead of averaging all four

module1.stem:
j = fh
The given equation relates the distinct positive numbers j, f, and h. Which equation correctly expresses f in terms of j and h?
module1.rationale: Multiplying both sides of j = fh by whatever divides f and dividing by whatever multiplies it gives f = j/h.
reasons: added the letters instead of multiplying them
turned the fraction upside down
multiplied every letter together instead of dividing

module1.stem: Ken needs at least 210 hours of flight time to get a private pilot certification. If Ken already has 126 hours of flight time, what is the minimum number of additional hours of flight time Ken needs to get a private pilot certification?
module1.rationale: The condition is 126 + n ≥ 210. With n = 84 the flight time is 210, which meets it, and with n = 83 it is 209, which does not, so the least whole number that works is 84.
reasons: reported the amount already accounted for rather than what is still needed
left the amount already accounted for out of the subtraction
added the two given amounts instead of subtracting them

module1.stem: The graph of the exponential function h is shown, where y = h(x). The y-intercept of the graph is (0, y). What is the value of y?
module1.rationale: The curve crosses the y-axis at (0, −4), so the y-intercept is (0, −4).

module1.stem: The y-intercept of the graph of y = 6x + 30 in the xy-plane is (0, y). What is the value of y?
module1.rationale: Putting x = 0 wipes out the term in x, and what is left is the constant term.

module1.stem: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to x² + 4x − 11 ?
module1.rationale: Half of 4 is 2, and (x + 2)² already carries 4, so −15 is what is left to reach −11.
reasons: added the correction instead of subtracting it
halved the middle coefficient with the wrong sign and corrected the wrong way too
halved the middle coefficient but changed its sign

module1.stem:
y < −x + 4
For which of the following tables are all the values of x and their corresponding values of y solutions to the given inequality?
module1.rationale: At x = 1 the boundary is 3, and only one table keeps every value of y on the required side of the boundary at all three values of x.
reasons: put every value of y on the wrong side of the boundary line
checked the pair at x = 1 and stopped; the other two lie on the wrong side of the boundary line
used y = −x + 4 itself, so every pair sits on the boundary line, which a strict inequality leaves out

assumed adding a constant stretches the data instead of sliding it

module1.stem:
(2p + 2)² − (5.2p² − 4)
Which of the following expressions is equivalent to the expression above?
module1.rationale: (2p + 2)² is 4p² + 8p + 4, and every term of the second bracket is then subtracted.
reasons: doubled each term instead of squaring and then added the two constants rather than subtracting
subtracted the two constant terms the wrong way round
doubled each term instead of squaring the binomial, so the middle term never appeared

module1.stem: A cargo helicopter delivers only 30-pound packages and 220-pound packages. For each delivery trip, the cargo helicopter must carry at least 9 packages, and the total weight of the packages can be at most 650 pounds. What is the maximum number of 220-pound packages that the cargo helicopter can carry per trip?
module1.rationale: Carrying 9 of the lighter packages weighs 270 pounds, and each swap to a heavier one adds 190 pounds. The cap leaves 380 pounds to spend on swaps, so at most 2 of the packages can be the heavier kind.
reasons: stopped one swap short of the weight the load allows
rounded the number of swaps up instead of down
near-miss arithmetic slip

module1.stem: If a is the mean and b is the median of thirteen consecutive integers, what is the value of |a − b| ?
module1.rationale: Consecutive integers are evenly spaced about their middle value, so the mean and the median are the same number.

module1.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to the expression (9vw)(v)(5w) ?
module1.rationale: The coefficients multiply and the exponents of v and of w each add, giving 45v²w².
reasons: added the three coefficients instead of multiplying them
multiplied the coefficients but added none of the exponents
added the exponents of v but left w alone

module1.stem:
3x + 7y = 26
27x + 63y = 234
For each real number r, which of the following points lies on the graph of each equation in the xy-plane for the given system?
module1.rationale: The second equation is the first multiplied by 9, so the two draw the same line and any point on it will do. Letting y be r and solving 3x + 7y = 26 for x gives every such point at once.
reasons: solved the equation for x but wrote that expression as the y-coordinate
solved for y but kept the sign of the x term, which changes the line
divided r by the multiplier between the two equations and used the two right-hand sides as the shifts

module1.stem: A circle has a radius of 19. What is the perimeter of a square whose area is equal to the area of this circle?
module1.rationale: The circle has area pi(19)^2 = 361π; a square of that area has side 19√π, so its perimeter is 76√π.
reasons: found the area as πr, forgetting to square the radius, and then took the square root
used the radius as the side length
used πr, forgetting to square the radius or take the root

module1.stem:
9, 9, 13, 13, 24, 24, 24, 24, 25, 25, 25
Which frequency table correctly represents the data listed?
module1.rationale: 9 appears 2 times, 13 appears 2 times, 24 appears 4 times, 25 appears 3 times.
reasons: multiplied each value by its count and then swapped the columns
swapped the two columns, reading each count as a data value
multiplied each value by how many times it appears instead of counting the appearances

module1.stem:
f(t) = t³ − 16t
g(t) = t² − 3t − 4
Which of the following expressions is equivalent to f(t)/g(t), for t > 4 ?
module1.rationale: t³ − 16t is t(t − 4)(t + 4) and t² − 3t − 4 is (t − 4)(t + 1), so only t − 4 cancels.
reasons: cancelled the wrong bracket and kept the one the denominator shares
cancelled the t in front as well as the shared bracket
cancelled everything in the numerator against the denominator

Data set A consists of 9 positive integers less than 68. The list shown gives 8 of the integers from data set A.
54, 60, 58, 59, 58, 54, 52, 53
The mean of these 8 integers is 56. If the mean of data set A is an integer that is greater than 56, what is the value of the largest integer from data set A?
module1.rationale: The 8 listed integers total 448. Only 65 makes 448 + x divide by 9 to give a whole number above 56.

module2_lower.stem: Which expression is equivalent to (3n + 2) + (4n − 2) ?
module2_lower.rationale: Like terms are collected power by power.
reasons: lined the terms up as written and added the exponents too
subtracted the constant terms instead of adding them
multiplied the coefficients of the like terms instead of adding them

module2_lower.stem: For a 6-week period in a town in Vermont, the lowest recorded temperature was 87 degrees Fahrenheit (°F) and the highest recorded temperature was 128°F. Which inequality is true for any recorded temperature t, in °F, in this town for this 6-week period?
module2_lower.rationale: Every recorded value is at least the smallest, 87, and at most the largest, 128; both were recorded, so both ends belong to the range and 87 ≤ t ≤ 128.
reasons: kept only the smallest recorded value and read it as a cap rather than as the bottom of the range
used the largest recorded value as the bottom of the range and the sum of the two as the top
kept only the largest recorded value and read it as a floor rather than as the top of the range

module2_lower.stem: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to 36j² − 1444 ?
module2_lower.rationale: 36 is 6² and 1444 is 38², so the expression is j times 6 all squared minus 38 squared.
reasons: used the same sign in both brackets, which squares the first bracket instead
halved the two square roots instead of taking them
halved the two square roots and used the same sign in both brackets

module2_lower.stem: A geologist estimates that the volume of a slab of basalt is greater than 17.2 cubic feet but less than 22.1 cubic feet. The geologist also estimates that the slab of basalt weighs 220 pounds per cubic foot of volume. Which inequality represents this situation, where x represents the estimated total weight, in pounds, of the slab of basalt?
module2_lower.rationale: Each cubic foot weighs 220 pounds, so the smallest total is 220(17.2) and the largest is 220(22.1); multiplying by a positive number keeps the two ends in order, so 220(17.2) < x < 220(22.1).
reasons: divided by the quantity that should have been multiplied, which also turns the two ends round
added the two quantities instead of multiplying them
subtracted the two quantities instead of multiplying them

module2_lower.stem:
5x² + 15x + 8 = 0
How many distinct real solutions are there to the given equation?
module2_lower.rationale: The equation has a discriminant of 65, so it has exactly two real solutions.
reasons: counted the two square roots of a positive number as a single solution
read the sign of the discriminant the wrong way round, and concluded that the curve never meets the axis
read the equation as an identity, true for every value of x

module2_lower.stem: For a party, 165 juice boxes are needed. Juice boxes are sold in packages of 24. What is the minimum number of packages that should be bought for the party?
module2_lower.rationale: The condition is 24n ≥ 165. With n = 7 the number is 168, which meets it, and with n = 6 it is 144, which does not, so the least whole number that works is 7.

module2_lower.stem: The graph of the polynomial function f is shown, where y = f(x). The y-intercept of the graph is (0, y). What is the value of y?
module2_lower.rationale: The curve crosses the y-axis at (0, −3), so the y-intercept is (0, −3).

module2_lower.stem:
u = wh
The given equation relates the positive numbers u, w, and h. Which equation correctly expresses w in terms of u and h?
module2_lower.rationale: Multiplying both sides of u = wh by whatever divides w and dividing by whatever multiplies it gives w = u/h.
reasons: multiplied every letter together instead of dividing
added the letters instead of multiplying them
turned the fraction upside down

module2_lower.stem: Which expression is equivalent to 5n² + 10n² + 8n?
module2_lower.rationale: 5n² and 10n² are the only like terms, so they combine and 8n stands alone.
reasons: treated all three terms as alike and added every coefficient and every exponent
multiplied the like terms instead of adding them, and added their exponents
combined the term that is not like the others with one of them

module2_lower.stem: The average annual energy cost for a certain home is $2,416. The homeowner plans to spend $24,000 to install a geothermal heating system. The homeowner estimates that the average annual energy cost will then be $1,338. Which of the following inequalities can be solved to find t, the number of years after installation at which the total amount of energy cost savings will exceed the installation cost?
module2_lower.rationale: Each year saves 2,416 − 1,338 dollars, so t years save (2,416 − 1,338)t, and that has to pass the $24,000 it cost to install, so 24,000 < (2,416 − 1,338)t.
reasons: subtracted one year's old cost from the installation cost instead of finding the yearly saving
divided the two annual costs instead of subtracting them
compared the two the wrong way round, so the saving never catches the installation cost up

module2_lower.rationale: The two arcs make up the whole circle, so the circumference is 48 + 240 = 288.

module2_lower.stem:
6, 7, 3, 18, 17
The mean of the list of numbers above is what fraction of the sum of the five numbers?
module2_lower.rationale: The mean is the sum divided by 5, so it is one fifth of the sum whatever the numbers are.

module2_lower.stem: Which expression is equivalent to (y)^(1/3), where y > 0?
module2_lower.rationale: An exponent of 1/3 is the cube root, so (y)^(1/3) is ³√y.
reasons: put the denominator of the exponent under the radical as a power instead of using it as the index
read the exponent as a coefficient
read the denominator of the exponent as a multiplier

module2_lower.stem:
y < 5x − 4
For which of the following tables are all the values of x and their corresponding values of y solutions to the given inequality?
module2_lower.rationale: At x = 3 the boundary is 11, and only one table keeps every value of y on the required side of the boundary at all three values of x.
reasons: put every value of y on the wrong side of the boundary line
used y = 5x − 4 itself, so every pair sits on the boundary line, which a strict inequality leaves out
checked the pair at x = 3 and stopped; the other two lie on the wrong side of the boundary line

module2_lower.stem: In the xy-plane, a circle with a radius of 14 has center (−11, 13). Which of the following is an equation of the circle?
module2_lower.rationale: A circle with center (h, k) and radius r has equation (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r², which gives (x + 11)² + (y − 13)² = 196.
reasons: kept the signs of the center and used the radius instead of its square
kept the signs of the center's coordinates instead of changing them
used the radius itself instead of its square

module2_lower.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to (y + z/4)² ?
module2_lower.rationale: (y + z/4)² is y² plus twice y·z/4 plus (z/4)², and squaring a fraction squares its denominator too.
reasons: forgot to double the middle term and squared only the numerator of the fraction
left out the middle term and squared only the numerator of the fraction
left out the middle term of the square

module2_lower.stem: A shipping service restricts the dimensions of the boxes it will ship for a certain type of service. The restriction states that for boxes shaped like rectangular prisms, the sum of the perimeter of the base of the box and the height of the box cannot exceed 200 inches. The perimeter of the base is determined using the width and length of the box. If a box has a height of 90 inches and its length is 3 times the width, which inequality shows the allowable width x, in inches, of the box?
module2_lower.rationale: The base has perimeter 2(x + 3x) = 8x, so 8x + 90 ≤ 200, leaving x ≤ 13 3/4; a width is positive, so 0 < x ≤ 13 3/4.
reasons: left the height out of the cap altogether
doubled the length but counted the width only once
added the width and the length once each instead of finding the whole perimeter

module2_lower.stem: Data set A consists of the distances of 28 trips and has a mean of 41 kilometers. Data set B consists of the distances of 77 trips and has a mean of 32 kilometers. Data set C consists of the distances of the 105 trips from data sets A and B. What is the mean, in kilometers, of data set C?
module2_lower.rationale: The two data sets total 1,148 and 2,464, so all 105 values total 3,612.

module2_upper.stem: Which expression is equivalent to (−2y − 9) − (2y + 5) ?
module2_upper.rationale: Like terms are collected power by power, and the minus sign in front of (2y + 5) applies to every term inside it.
reasons: multiplied the first expression by the negative of the second instead of subtracting
did not carry the minus sign as far as the constant term
applied the minus sign to its own answer's lower terms instead of to the second polynomial

module2_upper.stem: A geologist estimates that the volume of a slab of marble is greater than 13.5 cubic feet but less than 19.4 cubic feet. The geologist also estimates that the slab of marble weighs 225 pounds per cubic foot of volume. Which inequality represents this situation, where x represents the estimated total weight, in pounds, of the slab of marble?
module2_upper.rationale: Each cubic foot weighs 225 pounds, so the smallest total is 225(13.5) and the largest is 225(19.4); multiplying by a positive number keeps the two ends in order, so 225(13.5) < x < 225(19.4).
reasons: divided by the quantity that should have been multiplied, which also turns the two ends round
subtracted the two quantities instead of multiplying them
added the two quantities instead of multiplying them

module2_upper.stem: Which expression is equivalent to 676t² − 100 ?
module2_upper.rationale: 676 is 26² and 100 is 10², so the expression is t times 26 all squared minus 10 squared.
reasons: used the same sign in both brackets, which squares the first bracket instead
halved the two square roots instead of taking them
halved the two square roots and used the same sign in both brackets

module2_upper.stem: A cargo helicopter delivers only 160-pound packages and 230-pound packages. For each delivery trip, the cargo helicopter must carry at least 7 packages, and the total weight of the packages can be at most 1,500 pounds. What is the maximum number of 230-pound packages that the cargo helicopter can carry per trip?
module2_upper.rationale: Carrying 7 of the lighter packages weighs 1,120 pounds, and each swap to a heavier one adds 70 pounds. The cap leaves 380 pounds to spend on swaps, so at most 5 of the packages can be the heavier kind.
reasons: divided the weight left over by the heavier package rather than by the difference between the two
stopped one swap short of the weight the load allows
rounded the number of swaps up instead of down

module2_upper.stem:
(p³q³r⁶)(p³r⁶ + q⁹r⁻⁸)
Which of the following is equivalent to the expression above?
module2_upper.rationale: p³q³r⁶ multiplies each term inside the parentheses, and the exponents of each variable add.
reasons: kept only the variables that both factors carry, dropping q from the first product and p from the second
left q out of both products because it is missing from one factor of each
multiplied only the first term inside the parentheses by the monomial

module2_upper.stem:
56.54x + 18.10y = 1,088
Isabel ordered topsoil and crushed stone, which cost a total of $1,088, for her garden. The given equation represents the relationship between the number of cubic yards of topsoil, x, and the number of tons of crushed stone, y, Isabel ordered. How much more, in dollars, did a ton of crushed stone cost Isabel than a cubic yard of topsoil?
module2_upper.rationale: Each cubic yard of topsoil adds 56.54 to the bill and each ton of crushed stone adds 18.10, so the gap between the two per-unit prices is what is asked for.

module2_upper.stem:
x² − cx + 202 = 0
In the equation above, c is a constant and c > 0. If the equation has two integer solutions, what is a possible value of c ?
module2_upper.rationale: Two integer solutions multiply to 202, so they are 1 and 202, 2 and 101; c is their sum, which can be 103, 203.

module2_upper.stem:
2x − y ≥ 4
Which point (x, y) is a solution to the given inequality in the xy-plane?
module2_upper.rationale: Substituting x = 6 and y = 3 gives 2(6) − (3) ≥ 4, or 9 ≥ 4, which is true. Each of the other three points fails the inequality.
reasons: substituted the coordinates in the other order, putting the y-value in for x
read the inequality the wrong way round, so the region on the other side of the boundary looked like the solution
dropped a minus sign on a coefficient, which turns 2x − y ≥ 4 into 2x + y ≥ 4

module2_upper.stem:
(3w + 7)² − (w + 4) + 5(w + 3)
Which of the following expressions is equivalent to the expression above?
module2_upper.rationale: (3w + 7)² is 9w² + 42w + 49, and the minus sign in front of the second bracket reaches its constant too.
reasons: left out the middle term of the square
left out the middle term of the square and did not change the sign of the subtracted constant
did not change the sign of the constant in the bracket that is subtracted

halved the circumference instead of subtracting the given arc
gave the whole circumference instead of the remaining arc

module2_upper.stem: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to k² − 12k + 4?
module2_upper.rationale: Half of −12 is −6, and (k − 6)² already carries 36, so −32 is what is left to reach 4.
reasons: halved the middle coefficient but changed its sign
added the correction instead of subtracting it
halved the middle coefficient with the wrong sign and corrected the wrong way too

module2_upper.stem: A shipping service restricts the dimensions of the boxes it will ship for a certain type of service. The restriction states that for boxes shaped like rectangular prisms, the sum of the perimeter of the base of the box and the height of the box cannot exceed 190 inches. The perimeter of the base is determined using the width and length of the box. If a box has a height of 40 inches and its length is 3 times the width, which inequality shows the allowable width x, in inches, of the box?
module2_upper.rationale: The base has perimeter 2(x + 3x) = 8x, so 8x + 40 ≤ 190, leaving x ≤ 18 3/4; a width is positive, so 0 < x ≤ 18 3/4.
reasons: doubled the length but counted the width only once
added the width and the length once each instead of finding the whole perimeter
left the height out of the cap altogether

module2_upper.stem: The area of triangle ABC above is at least 96 but no more than 114. If y is an integer, what is one possible value of x ?

module2_upper.stem:
Data set A consists of 9 positive integers less than 43. The list shown gives 8 of the integers from data set A.
22, 31, 29, 22, 29, 22, 22, 31
The mean of these 8 integers is 26. If the mean of data set A is an integer that is greater than 26, what is the value of the largest integer from data set A?
module2_upper.rationale: The 8 listed integers total 208. Only 35 makes 208 + x divide by 9 to give a whole number above 26.

module2_upper.stem: The expression (u⁻³v^(1/3))/(u^(1/2)v⁻¹), where u > 1 and v > 1, is equivalent to which of the following?
module2_upper.rationale: Dividing subtracts the exponents, so u carries −7/2 and v carries 4/3.
reasons: added the two exponents of v the wrong way round
multiplied the exponents of u instead of subtracting them
multiplied the exponents of u and did not subtract the negative exponent of v

module2_upper.stem:
7x + 6y = 22
63x + 54y = 198
For each real number r, which of the following points lies on the graph of each equation in the xy-plane for the given system?
module2_upper.rationale: The second equation is the first multiplied by 9, so the two draw the same line and any point on it will do. Letting y be r and solving 7x + 6y = 22 for x gives every such point at once.
reasons: divided r by the multiplier between the two equations and used the two right-hand sides as the shifts
solved the equation for x but wrote that expression as the y-coordinate
solved for y but kept the sign of the x term, which changes the line

module2_upper.stem: Point O is the center of the circle above, the measure of angle ORS is 40°, and the radius of the circle is 30. What is the measure, in degrees, of angle ROS?

module2_upper.rationale: OR and OS are radii, so the triangle is isosceles and angle OSR also measures 40 degrees. That leaves 180 − 2(40) = 100 degrees at the center.
reasons: used the base angle as the central angle
doubled the base angle instead of subtracting twice it from 180
subtracted the base angle from 180 only once

module2_upper.stem: A botanist selected 100 seedlings at random from the seedlings in a greenhouse and randomly assigned them to two groups. One group was grown under a blue lamp for 3 weeks and the other under the usual lamp. The group grown under the blue lamp put on significantly more stem growth. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion from this study?
choices: The blue lamp causes an increase in stem growth for all seedlings of this species.
The blue lamp causes an increase in stem growth for the seedlings in this greenhouse.
The blue lamp causes an increase in stem growth for the 100 seedlings in the study.
There is an association between the blue lamp and an increase in stem growth for all seedlings of this species.
latex: The blue lamp causes an increase in stem growth for all seedlings of this species.
The blue lamp causes an increase in stem growth for the seedlings in this greenhouse.
The blue lamp causes an increase in stem growth for the 100 seedlings in the study.
There is an association between the blue lamp and an increase in stem growth for all seedlings of this species.
module2_upper.rationale: The seedlings were randomly assigned, so the difference between the groups is a cause; they were selected at random from the seedlings in this greenhouse, so the conclusion reaches that group.
reasons: generalized past the seedlings in this greenhouse, the group the seedlings were selected from
kept the conclusion inside the study although the units were selected at random from a whole group
generalized past the seedlings in this greenhouse, the group the seedlings were selected from

module2_upper.stem:
f(z) = z³ − 121z
g(z) = z² − 3z − 88
Which of the following expressions is equivalent to f(z)/g(z), for z > 11 ?
module2_upper.rationale: z³ − 121z is z(z − 11)(z + 11) and z² − 3z − 88 is (z − 11)(z + 8), so only z − 11 cancels.
reasons: cancelled everything in the numerator against the denominator
cancelled the z in front as well as the shared bracket
cancelled the wrong bracket and kept the one the denominator shares

In one week, Avery earned a total of s dollars for working at the two part-time jobs. added what each end of the line is worth instead of seeing that they are the same week's pay
priced the hours at job A at job B's rate

module2_upper.stem: In triangle RST, angle T is a right angle, point L lies on RS, point K lies on ST, and LK is parallel to RT. If the length of RT is 24 units, the length of LK is 6 units, and the area of triangle RST is 876 square units, what is the length of KT, in units?
module2_upper.rationale: The area gives ST = 2(876)/24 = 73. Triangle SLK is similar to SRT with ratio 6/24, so SK is that share of 73 and KT = 54.75.

module2_upper.topic_name: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Centre and Spread
module2_upper.stem: Data set A consists of the distances of 52 trips and has a mean of 33 kilometers. Data set B consists of the distances of 28 trips and has a mean of 63 kilometers. Data set C consists of the distances of the 80 trips from data sets A and B. What is the mean, in kilometers, of data set C?
module2_upper.rationale: The two data sets total 1,716 and 1,764, so all 80 values total 3,480.

module1.stem: For a 3-week period in a town in Illinois, the lowest recorded temperature was 30 degrees Fahrenheit (°F) and the highest recorded temperature was 54°F. Which inequality is true for any recorded temperature t, in °F, in this town for this 3-week period?
module1.rationale: Every recorded value is at least the smallest, 30, and at most the largest, 54; both were recorded, so both ends belong to the range and 30 ≤ t ≤ 54.
reasons: kept only the smallest recorded value and read it as a cap rather than as the bottom of the range
kept only the largest recorded value and read it as a floor rather than as the top of the range
used the largest recorded value as the bottom of the range and the sum of the two as the top

module1.stem: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to (4z + 7) − (5z + 1) ?
module1.rationale: Like terms are collected power by power, and the minus sign in front of (5z + 1) applies to every term inside it.
reasons: added the second polynomial instead of subtracting it
let the minus sign reach only the middle term of the second polynomial
applied the minus sign to its own answer's lower terms instead of to the second polynomial

module1.stem: Lena scored 71, 68, and 95 on the first three exams in history class. Solving which inequality gives the score, G, on Lena's fourth exam that will result in a mean score on all four exams of at least 85 ?
module1.rationale: The mean of the four scores is the sum divided by 4, and that mean has to be at least 85, so (G + 71 + 68 + 95)/4 ≥ 85.
reasons: subtracted the three known scores from the target mean instead of averaging all four
left the unknown score out of the sum being averaged
multiplied the unknown score by 4 instead of dividing the whole total by it

module1.stem:
c = 26jw
The given equation relates the positive numbers c, j, and w. Which equation correctly expresses j in terms of c and w?
module1.rationale: Multiplying both sides of c = 26jw by whatever divides j and dividing by whatever multiplies it gives j = c/(26w).
reasons: kept the coefficient on the side it started on instead of moving it across
wrote the whole right-hand side upside down
turned the fraction upside down

module1.stem: A geologist estimates that the volume of a slab of granite is greater than 22.7 cubic feet but less than 26.5 cubic feet. The geologist also estimates that the slab of granite weighs 220 pounds per cubic foot of volume. Which inequality represents this situation, where x represents the estimated total weight, in pounds, of the slab of granite?
module1.rationale: Each cubic foot weighs 220 pounds, so the smallest total is 220(22.7) and the largest is 220(26.5); multiplying by a positive number keeps the two ends in order, so 220(22.7) < x < 220(26.5).
reasons: subtracted the two quantities instead of multiplying them
added the two quantities instead of multiplying them
divided by the quantity that should have been multiplied, which also turns the two ends round

module1.stem:
|x − 6| = 5
What is the sum of the solutions to the given equation?
module1.rationale: The quantity inside the bars is 5 or −5, so x = 11 or x = 1.

module1.stem: Maria plans to rent a kayak. The kayak rental costs $50 per hour, and Maria will also have to pay for a life jacket that costs $20. Maria wants to spend no more than $440 for the rental and the life jacket. If the kayak rental is available only for a whole number of hours, what is the maximum number of hours for which Maria can rent the kayak?
module1.rationale: The condition is 20 + 50n ≤ 440. With n = 8 the cost is $420.00, which meets it, and with n = 9 it is $470.00, which does not, so the greatest whole number that works is 8.

module1.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to w² − 19 ?
module1.rationale: 19 is not a perfect square, but it is still √19 squared, so the expression is a difference of two squares.
reasons: used the same sign in both brackets, which gives a square rather than a difference of squares
looked for two whole numbers multiplying to −19 instead of taking a square root
used the same negative sign in both brackets

module1.stem:
y ≤ 2x + 1
For which of the following tables are all the values of x and their corresponding values of y solutions to the given inequality?
module1.rationale: At x = 2 the boundary is 5, and only one table keeps every value of y on the required side of the boundary at all three values of x.
reasons: put every value of y on the wrong side of the boundary line
the pair at x = 2 lies on the wrong side of the boundary line, although the other two are solutions
the pair at x = 8 lies on the wrong side of the boundary line, although the other two are solutions

The median of data set B is greater than the median of data set A, and the range of data set B is equal to the range of data set A.
The median of data set B is equal to the median of data set A, and the range of data set B is equal to the range of data set A.

module1.stem:
(2n − 2.4)² − (5.2n² − 6)
Which of the following expressions is equivalent to the expression above?
module1.rationale: (2n − 2.4)² is 4n² − 9.6n + 5.76, and every term of the second bracket is then subtracted.
reasons: doubled each term instead of squaring the binomial, so the middle term never appeared
doubled each term instead of squaring and then added the two constants rather than subtracting
subtracted the two constant terms the wrong way round

module1.stem: A cargo helicopter delivers only 50-pound packages and 120-pound packages. For each delivery trip, the cargo helicopter must carry at least 20 packages, and the total weight of the packages can be at most 1,600 pounds. What is the maximum number of 120-pound packages that the cargo helicopter can carry per trip?
module1.rationale: Carrying 20 of the lighter packages weighs 1,000 pounds, and each swap to a heavier one adds 70 pounds. The cap leaves 600 pounds to spend on swaps, so at most 8 of the packages can be the heavier kind.
reasons: stopped one swap short of the weight the load allows
rounded the number of swaps up instead of down
divided the whole weight allowance by the heavier package and ignored the smallest number of packages

module1.stem: Points P, Q, and W lie on a circle. Minor arc PQ has a length of 18 feet and major arc PWQ has a length of 72 feet. What is the circumference, in feet, of the circle?
module1.figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 216 216" width="216" height="216" role="img" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><style>.ax{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:1.4;fill:none}.gr{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:.5;opacity:.28}.pt{fill:currentColor}.sg{stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:1.4;fill:none}.lb{fill:currentColor;font:11px ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif}.it{fill:currentColor;font:italic 13px ui-serif,Georgia,serif}</style><circle class="ax" cx="108" cy="108" r="76"/><circle class="pt" cx="63.33" cy="46.51" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="58.04" y="36.23" text-anchor="end">P</text><circle class="pt" cx="152.67" cy="46.51" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="157.96" y="36.23" text-anchor="start">Q</text><circle class="pt" cx="108.0" cy="184.0" r="3.4"/><text class="it" x="108.0" y="205.0" text-anchor="middle">W</text></svg>
module1.rationale: The two arcs make up the whole circle, so the circumference is 18 + 72 = 90.

module1.topic_name: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Centre and Spread
module1.stem: If a is the mean and b is the median of fifteen consecutive integers, what is the value of |a − b| ?
module1.rationale: Consecutive integers are evenly spaced about their middle value, so the mean and the median are the same number.

module1.stem: Which expression is equivalent to (u⁻⁵v³w³)(u²w⁷ + v⁶w⁻⁵) ?
module1.rationale: u⁻⁵v³w³ multiplies each term inside the parentheses, and the exponents of each variable add.
reasons: multiplied only the first term inside the parentheses by the monomial
kept only the variables that both factors carry, dropping v from the first product and u from the second
left v out of both products because it is missing from one factor of each

module1.stem: A shipping service restricts the dimensions of the boxes it will ship for a certain type of service. The restriction states that for boxes shaped like rectangular prisms, the sum of the perimeter of the base of the box and the height of the box cannot exceed 215 inches. The perimeter of the base is determined using the width and length of the box. If a box has a height of 65 inches and its length is 3.5 times the width, which inequality shows the allowable width x, in inches, of the box?
module1.rationale: The base has perimeter 2(x + 3.5x) = 9x, so 9x + 65 ≤ 215, leaving x ≤ 16 2/3; a width is positive, so 0 < x ≤ 16 2/3.
reasons: added the width and the length once each instead of finding the whole perimeter
doubled the length but counted the width only once
used four widths, as though the base were a square

module1.stem: What is the side length of a square that has the same area as a circle with a radius of 28?
module1.rationale: The circle has area pi(28)^2 = 784π; a square of that area has side 28√π.
reasons: found the area as πr, forgetting to square the radius, and then took the square root
used the radius as the side length
used πr, forgetting to square the radius or take the root

module1.topic_name: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Centre and Spread
module1.stem:
9, 9, 9, 9, 14, 14, 23, 23, 23, 25, 25, 25, 25, 25
Which frequency table correctly represents the data listed?
module1.rationale: 9 appears 4 times, 14 appears 2 times, 23 appears 3 times, 25 appears 5 times.
reasons: multiplied each value by its count and then swapped the columns
multiplied each value by how many times it appears instead of counting the appearances
swapped the two columns, reading each count as a data value

module1.stem:
f(z) = z³ − 100z
g(z) = z² − 7z − 30
Which of the following expressions is equivalent to f(z)/g(z), for z > 10 ?
module1.rationale: z³ − 100z is z(z − 10)(z + 10) and z² − 7z − 30 is (z − 10)(z + 3), so only z − 10 cancels.
reasons: cancelled everything in the numerator against the denominator
cancelled the z in front as well as the shared bracket
cancelled the wrong bracket and kept the one the denominator shares

module1.stem: To earn money for college, Avery works two part-time jobs: A and B. She earns $10 per hour working at job A and $24 per hour working at job B. module2_lower.stem: During spring migration, a monarch butterfly traveled a minimum of 78 miles and a maximum of 107 miles between stopover locations. Which inequality represents this situation, where d is a possible distance, in miles, this monarch butterfly traveled between stopover locations during spring migration?
module2_lower.rationale: Every recorded value is at least the smallest, 78, and at most the largest, 107; both were recorded, so both ends belong to the range and 78 ≤ d ≤ 107.
reasons: kept only the largest recorded value and read it as a floor rather than as the top of the range
used the largest recorded value as the bottom of the range and the sum of the two as the top
kept only the smallest recorded value and read it as a cap rather than as the bottom of the range

module2_lower.stem: Which expression is equivalent to 576p² − 324?
module2_lower.rationale: 576 is 24² and 324 is 18², so the expression is p times 24 all squared minus 18 squared.
reasons: halved the two square roots and used the same sign in both brackets
used the same sign in both brackets, which squares the first bracket instead
halved the two square roots instead of taking them

module2_lower.stem: A geologist estimates that the volume of a slab of marble is greater than 22.6 cubic feet but less than 27 cubic feet. The geologist also estimates that the slab of marble weighs 100 pounds per cubic foot of volume. Which inequality represents this situation, where x represents the estimated total weight, in pounds, of the slab of marble?
module2_lower.rationale: Each cubic foot weighs 100 pounds, so the smallest total is 100(22.6) and the largest is 100(27); multiplying by a positive number keeps the two ends in order, so 100(22.6) < x < 100(27).
reasons: added the two quantities instead of multiplying them
subtracted the two quantities instead of multiplying them
divided by the quantity that should have been multiplied, which also turns the two ends round

read the sign of the discriminant the wrong way round, and concluded that the curve never meets the axis
read the equation as an identity, true for every value of x

module2_lower.stem: Ken plans to rent a kayak. The kayak rental costs $20 per hour, and Ken will also have to pay for a life jacket that costs $30. Ken wants to spend no more than $220 for the rental and the life jacket. If the kayak rental is available only for a whole number of hours, what is the maximum number of hours for which Ken can rent the kayak?
module2_lower.rationale: The condition is 30 + 20n ≤ 220. With n = 9 the cost is $210.00, which meets it, and with n = 10 it is $230.00, which does not, so the greatest whole number that works is 9.

reasons: multiplied every letter together instead of dividing

module2_lower.stem: What is the value of sin 145π/3 ?
module2_lower.rationale: 145π/3 and π/3 differ by whole turns, so sin 145π/3 = sin π/3 = √3/2.
reasons: gave the cosine of the angle instead
used the 45-degree reference value

module2_lower.rationale: 20j³ and 12j³ are like terms, so only their coefficients combine and the exponent is unchanged.
reasons: multiplied the coefficients instead of combining them
used the exponent as a factor on the combined coefficient
added the coefficients where the expression subtracts them

put every value of y on the wrong side of the boundary line

module2_lower.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to w² + 16w + 1?
module2_lower.rationale: Half of 16 is 8, and (w + 8)² already carries 64, so −63 is what is left to reach 1.
reasons: halved the middle coefficient with the wrong sign and corrected the wrong way too
added the correction instead of subtracting it

module2_lower.stem: A cargo helicopter delivers only 50-pound packages and 120-pound packages. For each delivery trip, the cargo helicopter must carry at least 14 packages, and the total weight of the packages can be at most 900 pounds. What is the maximum number of 120-pound packages that the cargo helicopter can carry per trip?
module2_lower.rationale: Carrying 14 of the lighter packages weighs 700 pounds, and each swap to a heavier one adds 70 pounds. The cap leaves 200 pounds to spend on swaps, so at most 2 of the packages can be the heavier kind.
reasons: stopped one swap short of the weight the load allows
rounded the number of swaps up instead of down
divided the whole weight allowance by the heavier package and ignored the smallest number of packages

module2_lower.stem: In the xy-plane, a circle with a radius of 8 has center (−9, −20). Which of the following is an equation of the circle?
module2_lower.rationale: A circle with center (h, k) and radius r has equation (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r², which gives (x + 9)² + (y + 20)² = 64.
reasons: used the radius itself instead of its square
kept the signs of the center and used the radius instead of its square
kept the signs of the center's coordinates instead of changing them

module2_lower.stem: Which of the following is an equivalent form of √(9u⁶v⁶)/u² ?
module2_lower.rationale: √(9u⁶v⁶) is 3u³v³, and dividing by u² subtracts 2 from the exponent of u.
reasons: halved the coefficient instead of taking its square root, and never divided by u²
used the square root of the coefficient as the root's index and divided each exponent by it

module2_lower.stem:
6x + 7y = 32
18x + 21y = 96
For each real number r, which of the following points lies on the graph of each equation in the xy-plane for the given system?
module2_lower.rationale: The second equation is the first multiplied by 3, so the two draw the same line and any point on it will do. Letting y be r and solving 6x + 7y = 32 for x gives every such point at once.
reasons: divided r by the multiplier between the two equations and used the two right-hand sides as the shifts
solved the equation for x but wrote that expression as the y-coordinate
solved for y but kept the sign of the x term, which changes the line

module2_lower.stem: A botanist recorded the species and the site of each of the 258 trees in a survey. What fraction of the birches and willows are at the south site? (Express your answer as a decimal or fraction, not as a percent.)
module2_lower.rationale: There are 114 birches and willows, and 63 of them are at the south site, so the probability is 21/38.

module2_upper.stem: Which of the following is an equivalent form of (−2t + 4) − (4t − 4) ?
module2_upper.rationale: Like terms are collected power by power, and the minus sign in front of (4t − 4) applies to every term inside it.
reasons: multiplied the first expression by the negative of the second instead of subtracting
changed the sign of only the first term of the second expression and then multiplied
did not carry the minus sign as far as the constant term

module2_upper.stem: A geologist estimates that the volume of a slab of limestone is greater than 6.9 cubic feet but less than 10.4 cubic feet. The geologist also estimates that the slab of limestone weighs 190 pounds per cubic foot of volume. Which inequality represents this situation, where x represents the estimated total weight, in pounds, of the slab of limestone?
module2_upper.rationale: Each cubic foot weighs 190 pounds, so the smallest total is 190(6.9) and the largest is 190(10.4); multiplying by a positive number keeps the two ends in order, so 190(6.9) < x < 190(10.4).
reasons: divided by the quantity that should have been multiplied, which also turns the two ends round
added the two quantities instead of multiplying them
subtracted the two quantities instead of multiplying them

module2_upper.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to the expression 196y² − 324 ?
module2_upper.rationale: 196 is 14² and 324 is 18², so the expression is y times 14 all squared minus 18 squared.
reasons: used the same sign in both brackets, which squares the first bracket instead
halved the two square roots and used the same sign in both brackets
halved the two square roots instead of taking them

module2_upper.stem: The average annual energy cost for a certain home is $2,820. The homeowner plans to spend $36,000 to install a geothermal heating system. The homeowner estimates that the average annual energy cost will then be $1,018. Which of the following inequalities can be solved to find t, the number of years after installation at which the total amount of energy cost savings will exceed the installation cost?
module2_upper.rationale: Each year saves 2,820 − 1,018 dollars, so t years save (2,820 − 1,018)t, and that has to pass the $36,000 it cost to install, so 36,000 < (2,820 − 1,018)t.
reasons: divided the two annual costs instead of subtracting them
compared the two the wrong way round, so the saving never catches the installation cost up
subtracted one year's old cost from the installation cost instead of finding the yearly saving

module2_upper.stem:
(a⁻⁶b³c³)(a³c⁶ + b⁹c⁻⁷)
Which of the following expressions is equivalent to the expression above?
module2_upper.rationale: a⁻⁶b³c³ multiplies each term inside the parentheses, and the exponents of each variable add.
reasons: multiplied only the first term inside the parentheses by the monomial
kept only the variables that both factors carry, dropping b from the first product and a from the second
left b out of both products because it is missing from one factor of each

module2_upper.stem:
57G + 11R = 419
At a school fair, students can win colored tokens that are worth a different number of points depending on the color. One student won G green tokens and R red tokens worth a total of 419 points. The given equation represents this situation. How many more points is a red token worth than a green token?
module2_upper.rationale: G is a count of green tokens, so the 57 multiplying it is the points one green token carries, and likewise 11 for a red one.

module2_upper.stem:
x² − bx + 50 = 0
In the equation above, b is a constant and b > 0. If the equation has two integer solutions, what is a possible value of b ?
module2_upper.rationale: Two integer solutions multiply to 50, so they are 1 and 50, 2 and 25, 5 and 10; b is their sum, which can be 15, 27, 51.

module2_upper.stem:
y < 5x − 6
For which of the following tables are all the values of x and their corresponding values of y solutions to the given inequality?
module2_upper.rationale: At x = 5 the boundary is 19, and only one table keeps every value of y on the required side of the boundary at all three values of x.
reasons: put every value of y on the wrong side of the boundary line
checked the pair at x = 5 and stopped; the other two lie on the wrong side of the boundary line
used y = 5x − 6 itself, so every pair sits on the boundary line, which a strict inequality leaves out

module2_upper.stem:
(y + 6)(y³ + 2)
Which of the following is equivalent to the given expression?
module2_upper.rationale: Every term of (y + 6) multiplies every term of (y³ + 2), and the two middle products are then collected.
reasons: subtracted the second expression instead of multiplying by it
added the leading coefficients instead of multiplying them
added the two expressions instead of multiplying them

module2_upper.stem: Which of the following is an equivalent form of p⁴ + 6p² − 72 ?

reasons: put the two signs on the wrong brackets
found a pair whose product is −72 but whose sum is 1, not 6
found a pair whose product is −72 but whose sum is −1, not 6

reasons: solved the equation for x but wrote that expression as the y-coordinate
divided r by the multiplier between the two equations and used the two right-hand sides as the shifts
solved for y but kept the sign of the x term, which changes the line

module2_upper.stem: Point M lies on a unit circle in the xy-plane and has coordinates (0, −1). Point C is the center of the circle and has coordinates (0, 0). Point N also lies on the circle and has coordinates (x, 1), where x is a constant. Which of the following could be the positive measure of angle MCN, in radians?
module2_upper.rationale: N must be (0, 1), the far end of the diameter through M, so angle MCN is a half turn plus any whole number of full turns: π + 24π = 25π.
reasons: a half-integer multiple of π stops a quarter turn away, at (1, 0)
an even multiple of π is a whole number of full turns, which ends back at M
a half-integer multiple of π stops a quarter turn away, at (−1, 0)

module2_upper.stem: A company selected 140 employees at random from its own employees and randomly assigned them to two groups. One group used a standing desk for 14 weeks and the other used a seated desk. The group that used the standing desk reported significantly greater comfort at work. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion from this study?
choices: The standing desk causes an increase in comfort reported at work for all office employees in the country.
There is an association between the standing desk and an increase in comfort reported at work for the 140 employees in the study.
The standing desk causes an increase in comfort reported at work for the employees of this company.
There is an association between the standing desk and an increase in comfort reported at work for all office employees in the country.
latex: The standing desk causes an increase in comfort reported at work for all office employees in the country.
There is an association between the standing desk and an increase in comfort reported at work for the 140 employees in the study.
The standing desk causes an increase in comfort reported at work for the employees of this company.
There is an association between the standing desk and an increase in comfort reported at work for all office employees in the country.
module2_upper.rationale: The employees were randomly assigned, so the difference between the groups is a cause; they were selected at random from the employees of this company, so the conclusion reaches that group.
reasons: generalized past the employees of this company, the group the employees were selected from
under-claimed twice over: random assignment earns a cause, and random selection earns the group the units came from
generalized past the employees of this company, the group the employees were selected from

module2_upper.stem:
f(z) = z³ − 9z
g(z) = z² + 3z − 18
Which of the following expressions is equivalent to f(z)/g(z), for z > 3 ?
module2_upper.rationale: z³ − 9z is z(z − 3)(z + 3) and z² + 3z − 18 is (z − 3)(z + 6), so only z − 3 cancels.
reasons: cancelled everything in the numerator against the denominator
cancelled the z in front as well as the shared bracket
cancelled the wrong bracket and kept the one the denominator shares

module2_upper.stem: Noor is working this summer as part of a crew on a farm, and earned $9 per hour for the first 15 hours worked this week. Because of that performance, the crew leader raised the salary to $15 per hour for the rest of the week. Noor saves 90% of the earnings from each week. What is the least number of hours Noor must work the rest of the week to save at least $400 for the week?
module2_upper.rationale: The condition is 0.9(135 + 15n) ≥ 400. With n = 21 the savings is $405.00, which meets it, and with n = 20 it is $391.50, which does not, so the least whole number that works is 21.
reasons: multiplied the target by the savings fraction instead of dividing by it
applied the savings fraction twice, once to the target and once to the hourly pay
used the first block's hourly rate for the whole week and left out the money already earned

module1.stem: During spring migration, a sandhill crane traveled a minimum of 26 miles and a maximum of 67 miles between stopover locations. Which inequality represents this situation, where d is a possible distance, in miles, this sandhill crane traveled between stopover locations during spring migration?
module1.rationale: Every recorded value is at least the smallest, 26, and at most the largest, 67; both were recorded, so both ends belong to the range and 26 ≤ d ≤ 67.
reasons: kept only the largest recorded value and read it as a floor rather than as the top of the range
kept only the smallest recorded value and read it as a cap rather than as the bottom of the range
used the largest recorded value as the bottom of the range and the sum of the two as the top

module1.stem:
(3t + 2) + (t + 1)
Which of the following is equivalent to the given expression?
module1.rationale: Like terms are collected power by power.
reasons: added the exponents as well as the coefficients
multiplied the coefficients of the like terms instead of adding them
added every coefficient and every exponent as if all the terms were alike

module1.stem: A geologist estimates that the volume of a slab of limestone is greater than 22.2 cubic feet but less than 25.1 cubic feet. The geologist also estimates that the slab of limestone weighs 100 pounds per cubic foot of volume. Which inequality represents this situation, where x represents the estimated total weight, in pounds, of the slab of limestone?
module1.rationale: Each cubic foot weighs 100 pounds, so the smallest total is 100(22.2) and the largest is 100(25.1); multiplying by a positive number keeps the two ends in order, so 100(22.2) < x < 100(25.1).
reasons: divided by the quantity that should have been multiplied, which also turns the two ends round
added the two quantities instead of multiplying them
subtracted the two quantities instead of multiplying them

module1.stem:
j = 60cr
The given equation relates the distinct positive numbers j, c, and r. Which equation correctly expresses c in terms of j and r?
module1.rationale: Multiplying both sides of j = 60cr by whatever divides c and dividing by whatever multiplies it gives c = j/(60r).
reasons: turned the fraction upside down
kept the coefficient on the side it started on instead of moving it across
wrote the whole right-hand side upside down

module1.stem: Devon needs at least 160 hours of flight time to get a private pilot certification. If Devon already has 64 hours of flight time, what is the minimum number of additional hours of flight time Devon needs to get a private pilot certification?
module1.rationale: The condition is 64 + n ≥ 160. With n = 96 the flight time is 160, which meets it, and with n = 95 it is 159, which does not, so the least whole number that works is 96.
reasons: reported the amount already accounted for rather than what is still needed
left the amount already accounted for out of the subtraction
added the two given amounts instead of subtracting them

module1.stem:
|x + 4| = 20
What is the positive solution to the given equation?
module1.rationale: The quantity inside the bars is 20 or −20, so x = 16 or x = −24.

module1.stem: The y-intercept of the graph of y = −6x − 28 in the xy-plane is (0, y). What is the value of y?
module1.rationale: Putting x = 0 wipes out the term in x, and what is left is the constant term.

module1.stem: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to p² − 19?
module1.rationale: 19 is not a perfect square, but it is still √19 squared, so the expression is a difference of two squares.
reasons: used the same sign in both brackets, which gives a square rather than a difference of squares
used the same negative sign in both brackets
looked for two whole numbers multiplying to −19 instead of taking a square root

module1.stem:
y > −2x − 1
For which of the following tables are all the values of x and their corresponding values of y solutions to the given inequality?
module1.rationale: At x = 1 the boundary is −3, and only one table keeps every value of y on the required side of the boundary at all three values of x.
reasons: put every value of y on the wrong side of the boundary line
used y = −2x − 1 itself, so every pair sits on the boundary line, which a strict inequality leaves out
checked the pair at x = 1 and stopped; the other two lie on the wrong side of the boundary line

module1.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to the expression (s + t/4)² ?
module1.rationale: (s + t/4)² is s² plus twice s·t/4 plus (t/4)², and squaring a fraction squares its denominator too.
reasons: left out the middle term of the square
forgot to double the middle term and squared only the numerator of the fraction
left out the middle term and squared only the numerator of the fraction

module1.stem:
H = 140p + 75
The formula above shows the relationship between Alice's target heart rate H, in beats per minute (bpm), and the intensity level p of different activities. When p = 0, Alice has a resting heart rate. When p = 1, Alice has a maximum heart rate. It is recommended that p be between 0.4 and 0.6 for Alice when training. Which of the following inequalities describes Alice's target training heart rate?
module1.rationale: The smallest the quantity can be is 75 + 140(0.4) = 131, and the largest is 75 + 140(0.6) = 159; the multiplier is positive, so the ends keep their order and 131 ≤ H ≤ 159.
reasons: multiplied the resting heart rate by each end of the range instead of adding the amount the rate builds up
left the resting heart rate out of both ends of the range
added the resting heart rate at the top of the range but not at the bottom

4, 17, 14, 7, 18, 10, 11, 2
The mean of the list of numbers above is what fraction of the sum of the eight numbers?
module1.rationale: The mean is the sum divided by 8, so it is one eighth of the sum whatever the numbers are.

module1.stem: Which of the following is an equivalent form of n⁴ − 8n² − 48 ?
module1.rationale: The constants in the two brackets have to multiply to −48 and add to −8; that second condition is what rules out the other factor pairs.
reasons: found a pair whose product is −48 but whose sum is −2, not −8
found a pair whose product is −48 but whose sum is 2, not −8
put the two signs on the wrong brackets

module1.stem: A team hosting an event to raise money for new uniforms plans to sell at least 370 tickets before this event and at least 180 tickets during this event to raise a total of at least $4,360 from all tickets sold. The price of a ticket during this event is $3 less than the price of a ticket before this event. Which inequality represents this situation, where x is the price, in dollars, of a ticket sold during this event?
module1.rationale: A ticket before the event costs 3 dollars more than one during it, so it costs x + 3 dollars, and the two groups together raise 370(x + 3) + 180x, which must be at least 4,360, so 370(x + 3) + 180x ≥ 4,360.
reasons: subtracted the difference from the earlier price instead of adding it
subtracted the difference from the earlier price and read the limit as a maximum instead of a minimum
read the limit as a maximum instead of a minimum

module1.stem: A square and a circle have the same area. If the diameter of the circle is 34, what is the perimeter of the square?
module1.rationale: The circle has area pi(17)^2 = 289π; a square of that area has side 17√π, so its perimeter is 68√π.
reasons: found the area as πr, forgetting to square the radius, and then took the square root
used the radius as the side length
used the diameter as the radius

module1.stem: The mean height of the 21 trees in an orchard is 48.5 feet. After the tallest tree is cut down, the mean height of the remaining 20 trees is 45.5 feet. What was the height, in feet, of the tree that was cut down?
module1.rationale: The 21 values total 1,018.5 and the 20 that remain total 910, a difference of 108.5.
reasons: reported how far the mean fell, not the value that was taken away
swapped the two counts, using one fewer for the original group
subtracted 21 times the new mean instead of 20 times

module1.stem:
f(n) = n³ − 36n
g(n) = n² + n − 42
Which of the following expressions is equivalent to f(n)/g(n), for n > 6 ?
module1.rationale: n³ − 36n is n(n − 6)(n + 6) and n² + n − 42 is (n − 6)(n + 7), so only n − 6 cancels.
reasons: cancelled the n in front as well as the shared bracket
cancelled the wrong bracket and kept the one the denominator shares
cancelled everything in the numerator against the denominator

module1.stem: A shipping service restricts the dimensions of the boxes it will ship for a certain type of service. The restriction states that for boxes shaped like rectangular prisms, the sum of the perimeter of the base of the box and the height of the box cannot exceed 255 inches. The perimeter of the base is determined using the width and length of the box. If a box has a height of 35 inches and its length is 3 times the width, which inequality shows the allowable width x, in inches, of the box?
module1.rationale: The base has perimeter 2(x + 3x) = 8x, so 8x + 35 ≤ 255, leaving x ≤ 27 1/2; a width is positive, so 0 < x ≤ 27 1/2.
reasons: added the width and the length once each instead of finding the whole perimeter
left the height out of the cap altogether
doubled the length but counted the width only once

module2_lower.stem: For a 3-week period in a town in Vermont, the lowest recorded temperature was 51 degrees Fahrenheit (°F) and the highest recorded temperature was 80°F. Which inequality is true for any recorded temperature t, in °F, in this town for this 3-week period?
module2_lower.rationale: Every recorded value is at least the smallest, 51, and at most the largest, 80; both were recorded, so both ends belong to the range and 51 ≤ t ≤ 80.
reasons: used the largest recorded value as the bottom of the range and the sum of the two as the top
kept only the smallest recorded value and read it as a cap rather than as the bottom of the range
kept only the largest recorded value and read it as a floor rather than as the top of the range

module2_lower.stem:
h = 59bf
The given equation relates the variables h, b, and f. Which equation correctly expresses b in terms of h and f?
module2_lower.rationale: Multiplying both sides of h = 59bf by whatever divides b and dividing by whatever multiplies it gives b = h/(59f).
reasons: kept the coefficient on the side it started on instead of moving it across
wrote the whole right-hand side upside down
turned the fraction upside down

module2_lower.stem: A geologist estimates that the volume of a slab of basalt is greater than 24.3 cubic feet but less than 25.8 cubic feet. The geologist also estimates that the slab of basalt weighs 270 pounds per cubic foot of volume. Which inequality represents this situation, where x represents the estimated total weight, in pounds, of the slab of basalt?
module2_lower.rationale: Each cubic foot weighs 270 pounds, so the smallest total is 270(24.3) and the largest is 270(25.8); multiplying by a positive number keeps the two ends in order, so 270(24.3) < x < 270(25.8).
reasons: added the two quantities instead of multiplying them
divided by the quantity that should have been multiplied, which also turns the two ends round
subtracted the two quantities instead of multiplying them

module2_lower.stem: Which expression is equivalent to 196j² − 484 ?
module2_lower.rationale: 196 is 14² and 484 is 22², so the expression is j times 14 all squared minus 22 squared.
reasons: halved the two square roots and used the same sign in both brackets
halved the two square roots instead of taking them
used the same sign in both brackets, which squares the first bracket instead

module2_lower.stem: Stefan plans to rent a boat. The boat rental costs $50 per hour, and Stefan will also have to pay for a water safety course that costs $25. Stefan wants to spend no more than $390 for the rental and the water safety course. If the boat rental is available only for a whole number of hours, what is the maximum number of hours for which Stefan can rent the boat?
module2_lower.rationale: The condition is 25 + 50n ≤ 390. With n = 7 the cost is $375.00, which meets it, and with n = 8 it is $425.00, which does not, so the greatest whole number that works is 7.

module2_lower.stem:
|x − 5| = 25
What is one possible solution to the given equation?
module2_lower.rationale: The quantity inside the bars is 25 or −25, so x = 30 or x = −20.

module2_lower.stem:
−2x² − 16x − 9 = 0
How many distinct real solutions are there to the given equation?
module2_lower.rationale: The equation has a discriminant of 184, so it has exactly two real solutions.
reasons: read the equation as an identity, true for every value of x
counted the two square roots of a positive number as a single solution
read the sign of the discriminant the wrong way round, and concluded that the curve never meets the axis

module2_lower.stem: What is the value of sin 517π/3, where the angle is measured in radians?
module2_lower.rationale: 517π/3 and π/3 differ by whole turns, so sin 517π/3 = sin π/3 = √3/2.
reasons: gave the cosine of the angle instead
used the 45-degree reference value
dropped the 2 in the denominator of the reference value

module2_lower.stem: Which expression is equivalent to 17d² + 20d²?
module2_lower.rationale: 17d² and 20d² are like terms, so only their coefficients combine and the exponent is unchanged.
reasons: subtracted the coefficients where the expression adds them
used the exponent as a factor on the combined coefficient
multiplied the coefficients instead of combining them

module2_lower.stem: The average annual energy cost for a certain home is $5,188. The homeowner plans to spend $16,500 to install a geothermal heating system. The homeowner estimates that the average annual energy cost will then be $2,246. Which of the following inequalities can be solved to find t, the number of years after installation at which the total amount of energy cost savings will exceed the installation cost?
module2_lower.rationale: Each year saves 5,188 − 2,246 dollars, so t years save (5,188 − 2,246)t, and that has to pass the $16,500 it cost to install, so 16,500 < (5,188 − 2,246)t.
reasons: divided the two annual costs instead of subtracting them
subtracted one year's old cost from the installation cost instead of finding the yearly saving
compared the two the wrong way round, so the saving never catches the installation cost up
