module2_lower.topic_name: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures of Centre and Spread
module2_lower.stem: If a is the mean and b is the median of nine consecutive integers, what is the value of |a − b| ?
module2_lower.rationale: Consecutive integers are evenly spaced about their middle value, so the mean and the median are the same number.

module2_lower.stem: Which expression is equivalent to (z)^(1/7), where z > 0?
module2_lower.rationale: An exponent of 1/7 is the seventh root, so (z)^(1/7) is ⁷√z.
reasons: read the exponent as a coefficient
put the denominator of the exponent under the radical as a power instead of using it as the index
read the denominator of the exponent as a multiplier

module2_lower.stem:
y < −x − 1
Which point (x, y) is a solution to the given inequality in the xy-plane?
module2_lower.rationale: Substituting x = −5 and y = −1 gives −1 < −(−5) − 1, or −1 < 4, which is true. Each of the other three points fails the inequality.
reasons: the point lies on the boundary line y = −x − 1, which a strict inequality leaves out
read the inequality the wrong way round, so the region on the other side of the boundary looked like the solution
dropped a minus sign on a coefficient, which turns y < −x − 1 into y < x − 1

module2_lower.stem: In the xy-plane, a circle with a radius of 13 has center (3, −5). Which of the following is an equation of the circle?
module2_lower.rationale: A circle with center (h, k) and radius r has equation (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r², which gives (x − 3)² + (y + 5)² = 169.
reasons: kept the signs of the center and used the radius instead of its square
used the radius itself instead of its square
kept the signs of the center's coordinates instead of changing them

module2_lower.stem: The number of seeds counted in 15 sample plots is summarized in the box plot above. Which of the following is closest to the first quartile of the numbers of seeds?

module2_lower.rationale: The box plot marks 120, 195, 255, 360 and 480, so the first quartile is 195.
reasons: read the end of the left whisker, the least value
read the right edge of the box, the third quartile, rather than the line inside it
read the end of the right whisker, the greatest value

module2_lower.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to a² + 10a + 9 ?
module2_lower.rationale: Half of 10 is 5, and (a + 5)² already carries 25, so −16 is what is left to reach 9.
reasons: halved the middle coefficient but changed its sign
halved the middle coefficient with the wrong sign and corrected the wrong way too
added the correction instead of subtracting it

module2_lower.stem: A shipping service restricts the dimensions of the boxes it will ship for a certain type of service. The restriction states that for boxes shaped like rectangular prisms, the sum of the perimeter of the base of the box and the height of the box cannot exceed 95 inches. The perimeter of the base is determined using the width and length of the box. If a box has a height of 75 inches and its length is 3.5 times the width, which inequality shows the allowable width x, in inches, of the box?
module2_lower.rationale: The base has perimeter 2(x + 3.5x) = 9x, so 9x + 75 ≤ 95, leaving x ≤ 2 2/9; a width is positive, so 0 < x ≤ 2 2/9.
reasons: doubled the length but counted the width only once
added the width and the length once each instead of finding the whole perimeter
used four widths, as though the base were a square

module2_lower.stem: The area of triangle ABC above is at least 60 but no more than 78. If y is an integer, what is one possible value of x ?

module2_lower.rationale: The area is 8y/2, so y is 15, 16, 17, 18, 19. The small triangle is similar to ABC, so x = 4y/8; y = 15 gives x = 7.5.

module2_lower.stem:
Data set A consists of 9 positive integers less than 40. The list shown gives 8 of the integers from data set A.
25, 29, 23, 24, 25, 31, 21, 30
The mean of these 8 integers is 26. If the mean of data set A is an integer that is greater than 26, what is the value of the largest integer from data set A?
module2_lower.rationale: The 8 listed integers total 208. Only 35 makes 208 + x divide by 9 to give a whole number above 26.

module2_upper.stem: Which expression is equivalent to (d + 1) − (4d − 2) ?
module2_upper.rationale: Like terms are collected power by power, and the minus sign in front of (4d − 2) applies to every term inside it.
reasons: did not carry the minus sign as far as the leading term
added the second polynomial instead of subtracting it
did not carry the minus sign as far as the constant term

module2_upper.stem: A geologist estimates that the volume of a slab of basalt is greater than 20.3 cubic feet but less than 23 cubic feet. The geologist also estimates that the slab of basalt weighs 280 pounds per cubic foot of volume. Which inequality represents this situation, where x represents the estimated total weight, in pounds, of the slab of basalt?
module2_upper.rationale: Each cubic foot weighs 280 pounds, so the smallest total is 280(20.3) and the largest is 280(23); multiplying by a positive number keeps the two ends in order, so 280(20.3) < x < 280(23).
reasons: divided by the quantity that should have been multiplied, which also turns the two ends round
subtracted the two quantities instead of multiplying them
added the two quantities instead of multiplying them

module2_upper.stem: Which of the following is an equivalent form of 324n² − 100 ?
module2_upper.rationale: 324 is 18² and 100 is 10², so the expression is n times 18 all squared minus 10 squared.
reasons: used the same sign in both brackets, which squares the first bracket instead
halved the two square roots instead of taking them
halved the two square roots and used the same sign in both brackets

module2_upper.stem: The average annual energy cost for a certain home is $5,654. The homeowner plans to spend $33,500 to install a geothermal heating system. The homeowner estimates that the average annual energy cost will then be $1,016. Which of the following inequalities can be solved to find t, the number of years after installation at which the total amount of energy cost savings will exceed the installation cost?
module2_upper.rationale: Each year saves 5,654 − 1,016 dollars, so t years save (5,654 − 1,016)t, and that has to pass the $33,500 it cost to install, so 33,500 < (5,654 − 1,016)t.
reasons: divided the two annual costs instead of subtracting them
compared the two the wrong way round, so the saving never catches the installation cost up
subtracted one year's old cost from the installation cost instead of finding the yearly saving

module2_upper.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to ⁸√(j² + 16j + 64), where j > 0?
module2_upper.rationale: j² + 16j + 64 is (j + 8)², and a root of index 8 divides that exponent by 8.
reasons: wrote the exponent as 1 over the index and forgot the 2 the square contributes
used the root's index as the exponent instead of dividing by it
factored the trinomial but never took the root

module2_upper.stem:
75.73x + 18.05y = 1,293
Isabel ordered topsoil and crushed stone, which cost a total of $1,293, for her garden. The given equation represents the relationship between the number of cubic yards of topsoil, x, and the number of tons of crushed stone, y, Isabel ordered. How much more, in dollars, did a ton of crushed stone cost Isabel than a cubic yard of topsoil?
module2_upper.rationale: Each cubic yard of topsoil adds 75.73 to the bill and each ton of crushed stone adds 18.05, so the gap between the two per-unit prices is what is asked for.

module2_upper.stem:
x² − rx + 225 = 0
In the equation above, r is a constant and r > 0. If the equation has two integer solutions, what is a possible value of r ?
module2_upper.rationale: Two integer solutions multiply to 225, so they are 1 and 225, 3 and 75, 5 and 45, 9 and 25, and so on; r is their sum, which can be 30, 34, 50, 78 and so on.

module2_upper.stem:
3x + 2y ≥ −2
−4x + 2y < −2
Which of the following ordered pairs (x, y) satisfies the system of inequalities above?
module2_upper.rationale: Substituting x = 4 and y = −6 gives 3(4) + 2(−6) ≥ −2, or 0 ≥ −2, and −4(4) + 2(−6) < −2, or −28 < −2, both of which are true. Each of the other three points fails at least one of the two inequalities.
reasons: substituted the coordinates in the other order, putting the y-value in for x
checked 3x + 2y ≥ −2 and stopped, without testing the other inequality
read both inequalities the wrong way round, so the region on the other side of the boundary looked like the solution

module2_upper.stem: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to (3y − 2.4)² − (5.2y² + 6)?
module2_upper.rationale: (3y − 2.4)² is 9y² − 14.4y + 5.76, and every term of the second bracket is then subtracted.
reasons: doubled each term instead of squaring and then added the two constants rather than subtracting
doubled each term instead of squaring the binomial, so the middle term never appeared
subtracted the two constant terms the wrong way round

halved the circumference instead of subtracting the given arc
gave the whole circumference instead of the remaining arc

module2_upper.stem:
9a² + 12ab + 4b²
Which of the following is a factor of the polynomial above?
module2_upper.rationale: 9a² is 3a squared, 4b² is 2b squared, and the middle term is twice their product, so the polynomial is a perfect square.
reasons: took the square roots of the variables but not of their coefficients
did not take the square root of the coefficient of a²
took the square root of neither coefficient

module2_upper.stem: Julissa is working this summer as part of a crew on a farm, and earned $10 per hour for the first 10 hours worked this week. Because of that performance, the crew leader raised the salary to $15 per hour for the rest of the week. Julissa saves 75% of the earnings from each week. What is the least number of hours Julissa must work the rest of the week to save at least $450 for the week?
module2_upper.rationale: The condition is 0.75(100 + 15n) ≥ 450. With n = 34 the savings is $457.50, which meets it, and with n = 33 it is $446.25, which does not, so the least whole number that works is 34.
reasons: multiplied the target by the savings fraction instead of dividing by it
applied the savings fraction twice, once to the target and once to the hourly pay
used the first block's hourly rate for the whole week and left out the money already earned

module2_upper.stem: The area of triangle ABC above is at least 36 but no more than 54. If y is an integer, what is one possible value of x ?

module2_upper.rationale: The area is 12y/2, so y is 6, 7, 8, 9. The small triangle is similar to ABC, so x = 8y/12; y = 6 gives x = 4.

module2_upper.stem: Data set A consists of the distances of 87 trips and has a mean of 43 kilometers. Data set B consists of the distances of 33 trips and has a mean of 29 kilometers. Data set C consists of the distances of the 120 trips from data sets A and B. What is the mean, in kilometers, of data set C?
module2_upper.rationale: The two data sets total 3,741 and 957, so all 120 values total 4,698.

module2_upper.stem:
f(w) = w³ − 9w
g(w) = w² + 7w − 30
Which of the following expressions is equivalent to f(w)/g(w), for w > 3 ?
module2_upper.rationale: w³ − 9w is w(w − 3)(w + 3) and w² + 7w − 30 is (w − 3)(w + 10), so only w − 3 cancels.
reasons: cancelled the wrong bracket and kept the one the denominator shares
cancelled everything in the numerator against the denominator
cancelled the w in front as well as the shared bracket

module2_upper.stem:
5x + 7y = 31
45x + 63y = 279
For each real number r, which of the following points lies on the graph of each equation in the xy-plane for the given system?
module2_upper.rationale: The second equation is the first multiplied by 9, so the two draw the same line and any point on it will do. Letting y be r and solving 5x + 7y = 31 for x gives every such point at once.
reasons: solved the equation for x but wrote that expression as the y-coordinate
solved for y but kept the sign of the x term, which changes the line
divided r by the multiplier between the two equations and used the two right-hand sides as the shifts

module2_upper.stem: A circle has a diameter of 24. What is the side length of a square whose area is equal to the area of this circle?
module2_upper.rationale: The circle has area pi(12)^2 = 144π; a square of that area has side 12√π.
reasons: found the area as πr, forgetting to square the radius, and then took the square root
used the radius as the side length
used the diameter as the radius

module2_upper.stem: An agronomist selected 40 plots at random from the plots on a farm and randomly assigned them to two groups. One group was given a new fertilizer for 7 weeks and the other was given the usual one. The group given the new fertilizer had a significantly higher yield. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion from this study?
choices: The new fertilizer causes an increase in yield for all the plots in the region.
The new fertilizer causes an increase in yield for the plots on this farm.
The new fertilizer causes an increase in yield for the 40 plots in the study.
There is an association between the new fertilizer and an increase in yield for all the plots in the region.
latex: The new fertilizer causes an increase in yield for all the plots in the region.
The new fertilizer causes an increase in yield for the plots on this farm.
The new fertilizer causes an increase in yield for the 40 plots in the study.
There is an association between the new fertilizer and an increase in yield for all the plots in the region.
module2_upper.rationale: The plots were randomly assigned, so the difference between the groups is a cause; they were selected at random from the plots on this farm, so the conclusion reaches that group.
reasons: generalized past the plots on this farm, the group the plots were selected from
kept the conclusion inside the study although the units were selected at random from a whole group
generalized past the plots on this farm, the group the plots were selected from

module2_upper.stem: The expression 24/(4p + 40) is equivalent to 6/(p + c), where c is a constant and p > 0. What is the value of c?
module2_upper.rationale: Dividing the numerator and the denominator by 4 turns 24/(4p + 40) into 6 over p + 10.
reasons: divided the constant by the new numerator instead of by the coefficient
reported the numerator instead of the constant
multiplied the two numbers in the denominator instead of dividing the constant by the coefficient

module2_upper.stem: A shipping service restricts the dimensions of the boxes it will ship for a certain type of service. The restriction states that for boxes shaped like rectangular prisms, the sum of the perimeter of the base of the box and the height of the box cannot exceed 150 inches. The perimeter of the base is determined using the width and length of the box. If a box has a height of 65 inches and its length is 1.5 times the width, which inequality shows the allowable width x, in inches, of the box?
module2_upper.rationale: The base has perimeter 2(x + 1.5x) = 5x, so 5x + 65 ≤ 150, leaving x ≤ 17; a width is positive, so 0 < x ≤ 17.
reasons: left the height out of the cap altogether
used four widths, as though the base were a square
added the width and the length once each instead of finding the whole perimeter

module2_upper.stem: In the figure shown, points Q, R, S, and T lie on line segment PV, and line segment RU intersects line segment SX at point W. The measure of ∠SQX is 61°, the measure of ∠SXQ is 77°, the measure of ∠SWU is 105°, and the measure of ∠VTU is 144°. What is the measure, in degrees, of ∠TUR?

module2_upper.stem: According to a set of standards, a certain type of glaze can contain a maximum of 0.25% lead by mass. If a sample of this glaze has a mass of 390 grams, what is the maximum mass, in grams, of lead the sample can contain to meet these standards?
